nodes.summary: The number $D_3(1)$ of partitions of $1$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $3$: the single part $1$ takes one of the three colors.
nodes.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $1$

nodes.summary: The number $D_3(2)$ of partitions of $2$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $6$: the single part $2$ in one of three colors, or two parts $1$ in two different colors.
nodes.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $2$

nodes.summary: The number $D_3(0)$ of partitions of $0$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $1$: the empty partition is the only one.
nodes.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $0$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $D_3(n)$ is the number of triples $(A, B, C)$ of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that the sum of the elements of $A$, the sum of the elements of $B$ and the sum of the elements of $C$ add up to $n$. Here $A$, $B$, $C$ are the parts of the three colors of a partition of $n$ whose parts of each color are distinct.
nodes.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $n$ and an overpartition $O$ of $n$, $\overline{\mathrm{mex}}_r(O)$ is the least positive integer $k$ that occurs fewer than $r$ times among the non-overlined parts of $O$. Such a $k$ exists, since $n + 1$ is not a part of $O$. For $r = 0$, which the paper does not use, the value is $0$ by convention.
nodes.title: Minimal excludant of an overpartition with a multiplicity bound

nodes.summary: For an overpartition $O$ of $n$ and a natural number $a$, the number of non-overlined parts of size $a$ in $O$ is the multiplicity of $a$ in the underlying partition of $O$, minus $1$ if $a$ is overlined in $O$ and minus $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Number of non-overlined copies of a part size

nodes.summary: The number $\overline{p}(0)$ of overpartitions of $0$ equals $1$: the empty overpartition is the only one.
nodes.title: The number of overpartitions of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\overline{p}(n)$ is the number of overpartitions of $n$, that is, of pairs consisting of a partition $p$ of $n$ and a set of overlined part sizes, each of which occurs as a part of $p$. For example, $\overline{p}(3) = 8$.
nodes.title: Number of overpartitions

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ be the sum, over all overpartitions $\pi$ of $n$, of $\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(\pi)$, the least positive integer that does not occur among the non-overlined parts of $\pi$. Then $\sigma\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(n) \sim e^{\pi\sqrt{n}} / (8 n^{3/4})$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, the ratio of the two sides tends to $1$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
